To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protein synthesis in yeast mitochondria is regulated by cytoplasmically made proteins, at least one of which exerts a specific effect on cytochrome c oxi-dase subunit synthesis.
cytoplasmic factors are required to maintain mitochondrial protein synthesis and that these factors are proteins that reside predominantly in the postribosomal supernatant.

the cytoplasmic protein factors that control yeast mitochondrial protein synthesis can be separated by centrifugation into a postpolysomal fraction and an 80 S ribosomal fraction and that the postpolysome fraction contains a factor that specifically stimulates the synthesis of subunit I-III of yeast cytochrome c oxdase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the regulation of protein synthesis within mitochondria and the elucidation of the mechanisms by which this regulation is achieved.
the regulation of protein synthesis in mitochondria by cytoplasmically derived proteins.
the study of the regulation of mitochondrial protein synthesis and has led to the discovery that cytoplasmic factors are involved in the regulation of this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of mitochondrial proteins is regulated at the translational level by cytoplasmically made proteins.
cytoplasmic protein synthesis in yeast is regulated at the translational level by a protein or proteins which act in a specific manner to control the synthesis of certain mitochondrial proteins.

cytoplasmically derived protein factors are required for the maintenance of mitochondrial protein synthesis and that the synthesis of at least one mitochondrial protein is regulated by a cytoplasmically encoded protein factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cytoplasmic stimulation of mitochondrial protein synthesis is mediated by a protein factor which appears to be a regulatory component of the cytoplasmic translation machinery.
cytoplasmic protein factors are required for the initiation of protein synthesis in yeast mitochondria.

the synthesis of at least a subset of yeast mitochondrial proteins is dependent on cytoplasmically derived protein(s) that are present within yeast mitochondria and that these protein(s) are not present at a sufficient level to support protein synthesis after isolation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytoplasmic factors are required for mitochondrial protein synthesis and that the cytoplasmic pool of these factors is depleted during the isolation process.
the synthesis of mitochondrial proteins is under cytoplasmic regulation and that the cytoplasm contains a pool of proteins that is necessary for the initiation of mitochondrial protein synthesis.
cytoplasmically derived proteins are required for protein synthesis in isolated yeast mitochondria.
